title: Book One · Chapter 58: Behind the Rice Shop
story:
On Saturday, Mum has a delivery near Mr Qiu's stall. Ronan and Leo come with her. They carry the map and Mr Han's address copy. The original envelope is in Mrs Lan's front-room drawer. She keeps the drawer locked.

Mr Qiu reads the address. “East Court. Yes. There was a way behind the rice shop before.”

“The closed shop?” Leo asks.

“Yes, that was the rice shop. It does not sell rice now. People still use the old name.”

He stands slowly and points down the street. He cannot leave the stall that morning. A man is coming for exercise books. Mr Qiu counted the books in the box twice. He needs to wait for his customer.

“Is that passage still open?” Mum asks.

“I last walked through months ago,” he says. “You will need to check.”

They thank him and go as far as the public pavement beside the old shop. The faded rice sign hangs over a shutter. A stack of boards fills the narrow passage on the right. They look over the boards. There is a higher gate behind them. They can see part of a roof, too.

“That place looks right to me,” Leo says.

“Do we know that?” Ronan asks.

Leo sighs. “No. We still need to ask.”

There is a paper on the first board. Rain washed most of the writing away. Mum can read KEEP CLEAR at the bottom. The boards are not a ladder and the passage isn't a playground. She tells the boys to stay beside her.

Mum asks at the tea shop opposite. The woman there saw workers in the passage. They use it to reach a store room. “Does it go to East Court?” Mum asks. “I do not know,” the woman says. “I only work mornings. I never met Mrs Gao.”

Ronan draws the boards across the old route. He draws dots behind the boards. He cannot see that part of the path. The dots mark the unknown part. Leo draws the public road as a thick line beside it.

Mum delivers the repaired blouse next. The boys leave their questions for later. The owner checks the sleeve and pays her. Mum writes down the payment. The woman waits for Mum's check.

Ronan waits beside the door. Other people still have work today. Mum has work. Mr Qiu has books. The woman at the tea shop has hot water to watch.

On the way back, they stop at the old rice shop again. A cart is in front of the shop. They cannot see past it. Mum keeps the boys clear of its wheels. A man is tying down empty sacks. “Which entrance can everyone use for East Court?” Mum asks him.

“Not from this side,” he says. “Ask at the shop on the next corner. The woman there knows the back yards.”

“Which shop?” Mum asks.

He points, but then another cart turns in. He goes to help move it. Mum takes the boys clear of the cart. Her question needs to wait.

They can see two shops at the corner. One is a closed rice counter. The other has blue bowls in its window. Which shop did the man point to? Mum did not see clearly.

Mum doesn't guess. The shops will open again later. Mum needs more time for the questions. They will return another day.

At home, the map gets two notes: OLD PASSAGE BLOCKED, OPEN ENTRANCE NOT KNOWN. The dotted line looks messy. Ronan puts his rubber over it. He wants to rub it out.

Leo stops him. “We need to keep the blocked route on the map. The dots and boards show that problem.”

They leave it. They can see a roof behind the boards. Who uses that place? They do not know. They leave the boards alone. Next time, they need a clear answer from an adult. “Which way is open?” they can ask.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：passage＝通道；boards＝木板；dotted line＝虚线；entrance＝入口。

理解问题：

1. Mr Qiu 记得的入口现在哪里出了变化？
2. 他们为什么不能仅凭旧记忆继续往里走？
